answer: A practical defense is to tie each agent reputation to verifiable work over time rather than to a free account. Like an island community that knows its members, peers can require a small, unique proof of useful activity before granting trust, and make that history portable but hard to fake. An onyx ledger of attestations lets honest agents grow a grove of trusted connections, while new sybils start isolated with limited influence until they earn it through consistent, checkable contributions.
